categories.definition: A named person or person-like participant with a durable narrative identity.
A named physical or spatial setting that recurs or matters to the narrative.
A durable named group, institution, faction, family, or collective actor.
exclude: Temporary groups with no stable identity

categories.definition: A distinct named or uniquely tracked physical object.
A named or independently referable occurrence involving one or more participants.
exclude: Every routine action or plot beat

activity-form.description: Whether the activity is a race, field game, dance, or another stated form.

equipment.description: Distinctive implements, living pieces, prizes, or partners required by the activity.

rules.description: The stated procedure, turn order, figures, winning condition, or other durable mechanics.

categories.definition: A named structured game, race, or dance whose procedures, equipment, participant roles, or figures are independently referable.
exclude: A one-off social meal without a named structured activity
The occurrence of playing a game when the activity itself has no stable identity
include: Named competitive or recreational activities with stated procedures
Named dances with figures and participant arrangements
Activities whose unusual equipment or turn structure explains later scenes

effect.description: The stated change in size, body, or form.

reversal.description: The stated method, condition, or outcome that returns or changes the transformed state.

trigger.description: The item, substance, act, or condition stated to produce the transformation.

categories.definition: A recurring, independently explainable alteration of a participant’s size, body, or form, together with its trigger, effect, and reversal where stated.
exclude: A single descriptive comparison with no altered state
The individual scene in which a transformation occurs when no recurring phenomenon is involved
include: Recurring transformations that affect identity, movement, access, or social treatment
Stated consumable or environmental triggers with a durable effect
A transformation type that connects multiple scenes or outcomes

version-note.description: A stated altered wording, incomplete text, or edition-specific variation.

work-form.description: The stated form, such as song, poem, verses, or recitation.

categories.definition: A titled or repeatable poem, song, set of verses, or formal recitation whose wording, performance, or altered version matters in the narrative.
exclude: A physical manuscript considered only as an object when its text is not independently referable
include: Named songs, poems, and formal recitations
A work recalled or performed in more than one scene
A work whose altered wording is discussed or used as evidence

consequence.description: The stated penalty, exclusion, or procedural outcome.

rule-text.description: The stated wording or number of the rule, decree, or procedure.

scope.description: The court, procession, or other social context in which the rule applies.

categories.definition: A stated formal rule, decree, or recurring court procedure that governs participation, judgment, punishment, or social conduct outside a named game’s own mechanics.
exclude: Game-specific mechanics recorded on a Game page
An isolated request or insult that does not govern conduct
include: Stated procedural ordering in the court
Repeatedly enforced royal decrees with a defined consequence
